data.title: Japan Tobacco to Book $8.6 Billion Loss on Russia Business
data.description:
By Kosaku Narioka

Japan Tobacco expects to book an $8.6 billion loss after losing control of its Russian business.

The Japanese tobacco maker said Thursday that it can no longer make business decisions concerning its operations in Russia in the same manner as before.

Earlier this month, Japan Tobacco said all seven of its Russian entities had been placed under temporary administration by a Russian company on the orders of President Vladimir Putin.

The move marked an escalation in Russian measures against Japanese businesses following Tokyo's support for Ukraine and its participation in Western sanctions against Moscow over its 2022 invasion.

Japan Tobacco on Thursday projected a net loss of Y724.00 billion, equivalent to $4.54 billion, for 2026, primarily due to a special loss of Y1.377 trillion related to the loss of control of its Russian business.

The company's Russian operations had about Y1.5 trillion in assets, including goodwill and roughly Y360 billion in cash and deposits, as well as about Y200 billion in liabilities at the end of September, the company said.

Japan Tobacco had expected Russia to account for about 10% of its revenue and 25% of adjusted operating profit in 2026.

The Japanese company was previously a state-owned monopoly, but the government held just under 38% of its shares at the end of 2025.

Japan Tobacco, whose brands include Winston and Camel, is one of Russia's largest tobacco companies, with a market share of nearly 40%.

Write to Kosaku Narioka at kosaku.narioka@wsj.com

data.title: Fed Credibility Seen Intact — Market Talk
data.description: The Federal Reserve's credibility looks intact because inflation expectations have barely moved even as policy-rate expectations rise, BNY's John Velis says in a note. "Markets still expect the Fed to address inflation, but the cost of maintaining credibility may be excessive restraint," the Americas macro strategist says. Velis adds that the rates markets' focus has become more specific, with an interest-rate hike in December being the main policy scenario markets are focused on, while the path beyond December is unclear. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

data.title: China expected to hold benchmark lending rates in November, but some see a cut coming
data.description:
China is set to leave benchmark lending rates unchanged in November for an 18th consecutive month, a Reuters survey showed, though a minority of respondents expect a cut, a departure from the unanimous calls for no change in previous months.

The loan prime ‌rate (LPR), normally charged to banks' most creditworthy clients in the world's second-largest economy, is calculated each month after 20 designated commercial banks submit proposed rates to the People's Bank of China (PBOC).

In a Reuters survey of 28 market ⁠participants this week, 23, or 82%, of all respondents predicted that the one-year ​ (CNYLPR1Y=CFXS) and five-year (CNYLPR5Y=CFXS) LPRs would stay unchanged at 3.00% and 3.50%, respectively, ​at Friday's review.

The other five expected a cut to one or both rates.

"We continue to view a November LPR cut as implausible and expect the PBOC to resume rate reductions with two 10-basis-point cuts in 2027 after staying on hold this year," Citi analysts said in a note.

However, the slight market expectations of additional monetary easing came after the central bank formally shifted its main policy rate to an overnight lending rate this month, a move analysts said ​would ease funding conditions and support the economy.

The change effectively lowered the floor of China's interest-rate framework by 15 basis points, reducing borrowing costs ​for financial institutions.

The PBOC also said it would shift the loan pricing benchmark from relying primarily on the LPR toward more diversified benchmarks, highlighting the overnight rate as an additional pricing reference.

Others say more stimulus may still be needed after China's economy showed fresh signs of sluggishness in October as factory production slowed and consumption remained weak, calling ​into question how long it can rely on exports to underpin growth.

data.title: Subscribe for Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd IPO; Geojit Financial Services
data.description:
Anand Rathi, Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd

Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL), incorporated in 1992 and headquartered in Odisha, is India’s single largest coal producer by output, accounting for 21.0% of domestic coal production and 28.4% of Coal India Ltd.'s production in FY26. The company primarily produces non-coking coal from the Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields (Odisha), serving power utilities and industrial customers across India. MCL benefits from a large reserve and resource base, providing long-term production visibility. Its highly mechanized mining operations, coal washery, and extensive rail-linked evacuation infrastructure support efficient and cost-effective production. As an owned subsidiary of Coal India Ltd., MCL plays a vital role in India’s energy security.

Valuation and Outlook

Further, the company has consistently rewarded shareholders through dividends, resulting in a 3-year average dividend yield of ~9.5% during FY24–FY26. Given its steady cash generation, strong balance sheet, long reserve life, and attractive dividend profile, we recommend SUBSCRIBE for investors seeking a high-quality dividend-paying stock with long-term visibility.

data.title: Seatrium's 3Q Order Wins Make for Decent Nine-Month Total — Market Talk
data.description: Seatrium's 3Q order wins contributed to a decent total for the nine months ended September, after a relatively dry first half, says Citi analyst Luis Hilado in a note. The offshore and marine company reported 1.9 billion Singapore dollars in order wins and indicated the potential for a project worth over S$2 billion in coming months, he says. Analysts during the post-announcement briefing appear concerned about order book replenishment, he notes. The company said the investment timings of deals in the pipeline remain subject to clients. "We believe the overhang of order win concerns can only find relief with fresh, significant wins", he says. Seatrium's full-year results print could also be a share-price driver, he says. Citi retains its buy rating and S$2.70 target price. Shares rise 0.6% to S$1.72. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
